source.title: An Educated Guess: Deriving Statistically Aligned Gradient Estimates for Zeroth-Order Optimisation
source.authors: Justus Huebotter; Serge Thill; M. van Gerven; Nasir Ahmad

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling affects the reported findings.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares gradient-based perturbation training with backpropagation and reports training outcomes on CIFAR-10 and Fashion-MNIST. This bears conceptually on V1, but does not test random-label memorization, CIFAR-100, or the claim's specified model-size and training-duration conditions.
record.gate_note: The paper measures gradient alignment and reports test or validation accuracy rather than training classification error. Its experiments therefore do not establish whether training error reaches zero or near zero. The reported methods, tasks, accuracy results and training comparisons are recorded below; cited results from prior work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates zeroth-order gradient estimators using gradient alignment and validation/test accuracy. It does not report training classification error, so neither its perturbation methods nor its backpropagation controls test V1. It also reports no comparisons testing V2–V6. The record's tests/T2 classification and V1 tested_not_extracted status should be corrected.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that activation-informed SZO estimators improve gradient alignment and enable learning on Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10. They recommend SZO-1 when only weights can be perturbed, while acknowledging that its advantage over NP on their CNN holds with SGD but not SOAP.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates forward-only zeroth-order gradient estimators, including SZO, against backpropagation, using accuracy outcomes rather than training classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with dataset and architecture, perturbation method, number of probes, batch versus per-sample credit, optimiser, activation awareness, learning rate, spectral exponent and iterative versus simultaneous layer perturbation.

fits_no_version.finding: SZO estimators improve alignment with backpropagation gradients relative to isotropic weight perturbation at initialization (Figure 1; Appendices J–K).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shaping zeroth-order search directions using activation geometry can improve gradient-estimation alignment.

fits_no_version.finding: SZO-1 outperforms weight perturbation in reported accuracy comparisons and leads node perturbation on the CIFAR-10 CNN with SGD and Adam; SOAP instead gives NP and NTWP the highest accuracies (Section 6; Appendix L). These are held-out accuracy outcomes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-informed zeroth-order estimators can improve held-out classification accuracy over conventional perturbation methods, with rankings depending on architecture and optimizer.

fits_no_version.finding: Simultaneous perturbation reduces CIFAR-10 validation accuracy relative to iterative perturbation: SZO-1 reaches 35% versus 46%, and SZO-infinity 33% versus 44% (Appendix N). This compares probing modes at fixed architecture, rather than depth or identity shortcuts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Perturbing layers individually can improve zeroth-order training outcomes at additional computational cost.

record.problems: The experiments report test or validation accuracy, not training classification error, so they do not directly answer whether models reach zero or near-zero training error. Main training experiments use a two-layer Fashion-MNIST MLP and a six-layer CIFAR-10 CNN; no CIFAR-100 or label-corruption experiments are reported. Some results are figure-only in the supplied text, and numerical values cannot be recovered from those plots.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows: although the paper reports many accuracy outcomes, these are outcomes of its zeroth-order training methods and do not measure the training-error behavior named in V1. The study does not test V2–V6.

untested.parts: All: no training classification error is reported, including for the CIFAR-10 backpropagation controls; no CIFAR-100, random-label, corrupted-label, or training-error comparisons across model sizes or stopping conditions.
All: no two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment, spurious-minimum frequency, or extra-student-neuron comparison.
All: no training-error comparison across network depths or identity-shortcut conditions.
All: no comparison of initialization schemes for learning speed or trainable depth. Appendix A invokes initialization theory to motivate a gradient prior.
All: no initial linearized stability threshold, curvature trajectory, catapult recovery, or edge-of-stability measurement.
All: no batch-normalization comparison or Fixup experiment; the experimental networks contain no normalization layers.

record.verdict_notes: Keeping the result rows empty is appropriate for these six versions. The unrelated accuracy and alignment outcomes are already declared in rows_left_out; no missing claim-relevant result requires extraction. Low held-out accuracy does not establish substantial training error, and successful held-out learning does not establish near-zero training error.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report training classification error, random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-100, or comparisons of model size and early stopping against training error.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
